description: Many distributed/consensus systems separate ingestion/persistence from semantic validation (e.g., EVM execution, signature verification, state-machine application). If the durability boundary is not atomic, crashes can leave “half-ingested” items that look complete enough to be rediscovered. A common bug is a fast-path that returns “valid/accepted” when the item is present in storage, without checking a durable validation-status bit or re-executing validation. This can launder invalid items into the “valid” set and even into canonical state, violating safety/agreement and often causing liveness failure (node wedges on an invalid head).
fault_type: crash_recovery / torn_persistence (non-atomic durability across validation boundary)
trigger_condition: - The implementation persists “presence” artifacts for an object (block/proposal/log entry) before persisting a durable validation outcome.
